sn35.246:1.1: The same five defilements are listed at [mn151:3.3]().
sn35.246:3.3: The _ghaṭā_ (“pot”) is the prominent hump of a zebu bull, which is grabbed to this day by bull wranglers.
sn35.246:4.18: Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 2.4.9 says you can only catch the sound of a harp by getting hold of the lute or player, using this as a metaphor for the search for the Self. [dn23:19.3]() tells a similar parable, only with a horn. The Upaniṣad has both instruments.
sn35.246:4.24: The rare verb _samanvesati_ is used in [sn4.23:10.4]() and [sn22.87:11.5]() of Māra “searching” for the consciousness of a deceased arahant.
